reviews.text: Once again, Moi Rai comes up with a fantastic answer to the question: "Wouldn't it be cool if Pokemon had combat that was actually deep and interesting?"

I CAN FINALLY TALK ABOUT THIS GAME!!! Beta tested for Aethermancer and absolutely in love with the game! Even in Early Access, there's so many different ways to play that I can just pick it up, play a run and test out something new. With the right traits and actions, you can reach some very absurd heights that just feel so good to hit. If you are a fan of exponential power scaling, stunning animation, wonderful monster designs and experimental team building, I very much recommend picking up Aethermancer! (Going to be buying it for some of my friends too, so they're not safe either.)

Aethermancer! Moi Rai's at it again, with another complex teambuilding monster tamer game! Except this time, it's a roguelite! As a completely and totally and extremely unbiased alpha/betatester, I'd gladly say the game is awesome and if you like teambuilding games, you should definitely get this one, even if monster tamers aren't really your thing. At the time of review, the game just hit early access. Even then, there's already several full runs worth of content--3 biomes, 1 final boss, 28 monsters + shifting/shiny mechanic, difficulty adjustments/ascension ranks, and some toggles in the options to make mechanics easier. Generally speaking, if you played Monster Sanctuary, you'll find the teambuilding and general gameplay to be familiar. Not 100% the same, but very familiar. As a game, AE definitely feels like an iteration and refinement from what they learned off MS.

2025年是荒野，优米雅，和以太术士。 前作怪物圣所100小时全成就实在不想把这游戏与上面两个放一块，但在让人失望方面毫无疑问，它做到了。 不推荐除了怪物圣所极端粉丝外的人购买，一想到每一份支持都在帮助作者放飞自我就想笑。 —————————————————————————————————————————————————— 1 肉鸽与地图探索的结合玩起来简直是左右脑互博 地图做的非常鸡肋，与其让我在那地图上上蹿下跳为了那几个金币，不如直接做成爬塔的路线选择，不仅更直观而且更方便。请告诉我跳跃设计除了高对低多打一层（更显鸡肋）外还有什么用？ 看的出来在地图上是做了一些无用功设计，比如蜘蛛网，罐头，部分建筑描述，有碎片化叙事的想法在里面，但别忘了，这游戏本质依然是肉鸽游戏，有多少人会在意你在哪个犄角旮旯塞了什么奖励和背景补充？反正我只想快点收集奖励进入下一场战斗。 2节奏拖沓就如同老奶奶的裹脚布又臭又长 你以为无聊的地图探索已经是这游戏的全部了吗？恰恰相反！这仅仅只是开胃小菜！作为一个2025年的游戏，居然没有倍速，何意味？一局游戏你要花1/3的时间在地图上犹如猴子一般上蹿下跳，1/2的时间要看技能特效！年龄，反击，施加状态，进攻防御特效，作者细心的做了非常多技能特效，毫无疑问这是好的，但它忘了添加倍速按钮，就像吃夏威夷果但是忘了给你工具....... 3平平无奇的宠物培养 前作一个非常大的亮点特色就是宠物的分支培养，而在这里缺几乎很少看出差异性。宠物异化变成了特性的3选一变化，只要常驻的2足够满足需求，很多时候是不是异化区别不是很大。同时将被动放在等级奖励也直接淡化了宠物养成的快乐，沿用以前的思路特定等级出现进化分支至少会比现在有点意思。 4失败的肉鸽部分 宠物收集越多，你越弱。很难平，但这就是事实。除了初始自带后续选取是在全部池子随机，然而你只有一次刷新机会，这就导致了游戏都要结束了还在找宠物。 与之相对应的是只要两次的升级刷新机会。一如前面所说，宠物一共3特性，如果是两个特性没重合的宠物，那么升级特性技能池子就会变的很乱，经常是史海遨游 在此基础上，这游戏没有图鉴！ 有一个肉鸽游戏也没图鉴，但人家叫以撒。 5装备 没啥好说的，这作仅能穿戴一个装备，可玩性大幅度降低. 下面是私货环节 我觉得有一个游戏非常有意思----超时空方舟 如果将宠物和调查员一样视为可操作角色，那事情就变得有趣多了 一样有大地图探索，但是超舟取而代之能直接传送到对应怪物/事件。同时地图有隐藏宝箱的额外能让人有慢慢探索的欲望 一样需要多名可操作角色但超舟是出门2加后续两次选人，并且支持少人通关 一样升级面板提升并获得新技能/卡牌 一样有装备栏不过是2个 可以说除了战斗部分是卡牌，肉鸽和RPG的元素都有相似

I bought Aethermancer on a whim and WOW am I happy I did! This game is truly a perfect blend of Binding of Isaac (randomly generated maps + hardcore roguelike elements + slowly building your progression from experimental runs) AND Pokemon (creature taming + creature progression) in a way that I never knew I needed. All I can hope is that continuous content is released because this will be a staple game for years to come for ANY Pokemon-style fan AND/OR any Roguelike fan. Gameplay 11/10 Music 7/10 Graphics 6/10 Creativity 10/10 Will update once I have completed all content in game.

For an early access game, it's solid. For a demo, it's amazing. But for $22 it absolutely needs work to bring itself up to that value. What it does, it does right. The monster designs are cool, the music is fantastic, the art style is great, and the game feels like it has polish, it just needs to do way more of those things. There aren't quite enough monsters in each world to make successive runs feel unique to the last. You end up trying to do the same exact thing again but better, against way too many of the exact same groups from your last run, which isn't really how a roguelite should function. I was drawn to this as "doing what pokemon does but better" but at the end of the day it's no different than Pokemon's gameplay of mashing A to keep repeating the same actions over and over. The maps having some random generation to layout isn't enough variety to carry a game like this. There needs to be more monsters, more variety to the maps or the ability to skip a world if you've beaten it enough times (or just let me decide where I want to go), and more balancing so you're not just making the same squads every single run. In its current state, I can't recommend this game at $22, there's just not that much meat yet. /edit disabling comments because for some reason the fact that I dislike the game hurt people's feelings? lol

I'm not really a "review" kind of guy, but I owe it to this company for the sheer amount of hours I've dumped into their catalog. It's also my first review, so that should speak volumes. As a heads up, Minor spoilers ahead for gameplay and unlockables. The game (as of time of writing) is in early access and it shows, both good and bad. A lot of extremely well developed ideas, art, and gameplay is on full display, but there is definitely room for improvement. I, as of time of writing, have everything unlocked/bought and an excess of retained resources and I do play with default corruption. I'll start with the negatives. -Non-combat exploration feels good in small doses, but tends to overstay its welcome after all monsters on a map are clear and the ability to fast travel to an otherwise discovered exit isn't possible. I'm not sure if that is a bug. -The map generation sometimes puts near invisible obstacles on the ground that are a bit frustrating to deal with. -Non-combat exploration's dash doesn't [i] feel [/i] enough. Overworld monsters have a very forgiving "leash" time, and walking is more than enough. The dash stopping at a ledge I'm trying to jump down doesn't feel the best, nor does the linked dash between elevated platforms feel consistent. -(Some) NPCs are filled with lore, but "interaction" on a non-lore basis is minimal. -The only negative I have about actual gameplay (combat) is a general note on balance. I do want to say full-throatedly that balance is hard when there is as much depth that the devs are trying to achieve, but they've absolutely knocked it out of the park with previous titles. With that said-- --I never felt that really strong team comps required equipment or artifacts and that build/run defining traits/attacks were spread out across the monsters of that team such that I could reliably complete the game without worry. --Some middling comps are make/break and require many more defining traits or abilities or that only 1/3 of the monsters actually get the build defining skills or require a significant amount of luck to get passable equipment. I've scrapped many runs after struggling to get to the third area. --Some comps, even with shared non-tank archetypes don't feel like they jive well or that it takes significant work, planning, and luck to advance. --Incoming damage can feel extremely lopsided and grow faster than your mitigation. I've intentionally avoided using tanks as proper tanks in recent history. Tanks generally don't feel beefy enough even with intentionally stacking shield/avoidance/damage reduction later in the game. --Unlike some other roguelites, what I would call "player skill" has a much lower ceiling. Much more feels like a product of RNG. --The game, as a whole seems slow when I want it to be faster(the series of a hundred procs per turn), and fast when I want it to be slow (no transition/confirmation on item buy). With the entirety of all negative things I have to say out of the way, let's move on to the positives! -Build diversity is absolutely insane, especially with all of the QOL benefits that can be unlocked between runs. Even "bad" setups can be mostly passable until the third area with judicious artifact usage. -The monster design is top notch, even the shifted variants provide a different vibe and matches very well with the difference in archetype across variants. -The gameplay (if this is your shtick) is addictive. The loop is simple, like most roguelikes, but the difference in depth when you can't guarantee your team comps and you can really push a hodgepodge of thematically/archetypically clashing (on the surface) monsters into a cohesive win-con is something else. There's only 2 "must-haves" for maybe 3 different setups that I would consider "easy mode". Past that, I would never think that I am "owed" a win for a given team comp. -The lore, the pieces that exist, are fantastic and a very solid foundation to keep building a more cohesive world that feels much more alive. -The dev team. That's it. This team has pumped out some exceptional content and supported their previous titles well past a "reasonable" time after release/DLC roll-outs. While the number of negatives outweighs the number of positives, this is still very much a game that I will be playing in its current state, through EA, and beyond any content release. What this game does, it does exceptionally well, and you can see where the dev team has put scaffolding/framework in to further build this game for future content.

from start to finish, I couldn't put Monster Sanctuary down. It was an absolute gem and scratched all the right spots for me. I *want* to like Aethermancer. Maybe (quite possibly) it's just me and I'm giving the game negativity based on my own shortcomings, but I've yet to do a run in this game that left me wanting to play more. Maybe there's a proper update or two in the future that could revamp the system a bit, but for the time being it just doesn't hit enough marks for me to say I enjoy it all that much.

While I do like the game and think it has potential, it is too tedious in its current state. There is an overworld for whatever dumb reason and it doesn't add any depth to the game. It just makes it more tedious to play. You're forced to walk around in an overworld during your runs simply for the sake of adding more "depth." It wouldn't be an issue, but there is almost no reason for this. It would be infinitely more enjoyable if we just had a map to select our stages from and skip the walking around simply for the sake of smashing boxes and clicking on stuff for a small amount of gold. This is not the type of game designed for this and it really impacts how enjoyable it is. Constantly running through the maps trying to make sure you collected all the miniscule amounts of gold and checking the map really ruins the immersion. Genuinely confused as to why this is a feature in a game like this.

I've enjoyed Aethermancer for the most part, but there are certainly parts that don't mesh well with me and feel a bit unpolished and awkward. I enjoy creature collecting and roguelike, and when I learned that this game combines the two, I was very intrigued. I remember watching the trailer and some YouTubers play the game, and thought I would really enjoy this, especially with how great the pixel art looked. After playing a couple hours of the game, it was clear to me what I liked and disliked. In terms of positives (aside from visuals/fx), I really enjoyed the snappy moment to moment turn-based combat. I felt like the elemental system was well made, there was enough playstyle expression - enough for players to try out different movesets and equipments, but also enough for players to hard force a playstyle or team if desired. The controls felt easy to pick up and the turn-based combat turned out to flow really well. I enjoyed dishing out a flurry of attacks, staggering monsters with a strategic setup, and leveling up my monsters to learn new moves. Unfortunately, that's kinda where my positives end for the gameplay. Personally, I wasn't a fan of a lot of the directions the devs took with the overworld gameplay and non-combat related decisions. Right now, the overworld feels a bit dead - it's clear that each floor has a set of rooms, and it feels awkward having to walk to each one, break all the boxes, and have to traverse up and down layers to make sure i don't miss anything. Additionally, I feel like the difficulty ramp around world 2-3 ramp up super hard, and I've had trouble with both corruption and just the monsters hitting SUPER hard. After like 3-4 runs, I have had them all end not from the bosses, but just the normal creeps around the map, and it would often happen when one of my monsters dies, and I would just bleed up slowly. And this is all with me heavily investing in a healer and tank in most runs. This could really just be a skill issue, but I felt like I didn't feel that sense of progression yet, and after several runs, the meta progression outside of the game didn't really alter my team too much to make a difference. I still think the game is well worth the money and maybe it just didn't click with me enough to REALLY enjoy it. But after playing other roguelites, such as Balatro, Ravenswatch, Shape of Dreams, Slay the Spire, Hades, and even like PEAK... i felt like those games helped me progress much smoother and I felt like I "GOT IT" after it a bit. Even with a game like Chaos Zero Nightmare, which is a gacha roguelite deckbuilder, I feel that game ramped up the player much better. So yes, I'm recommending this game on its future and its potential to be great. I think it's worth it if you really like this kind of monster collecting roguelite, but I am bothered by some of the elements that prevent me from fully enjoying it. 6/10

Family was all busy and scheduling messy, so I was alone for Christmas. This game kept me good company. I have to say, this stands out as having a pretty strong gameplay loop. Game has very interesting bones. In all honesty I'm torn regarding the rating. There's something missing in the balance and progression to make it feel fair - randomness in monster traits and active skills make it challenging to be consistent (at least without lots of upgrades). Some monster groups also feel plain unfair, clearly as other reviews stated certain builds or ways of playing are favored, which dilutes the potential the devs created. (edit) I initially decided to give the game a thumbs up with the trust that it will develop into something great. Since then I've faced the final boss and let me tell you about an unbalanced experience. Left a sour taste in my mouth. Not fond of having to build a team specifically against certain mechanics to be able to progress.

the open ended fun exploration) into a roided up version of itself, these devs are "Obsessed" with Buffs/Debuffs, and the visual vommit onscreen that comes with that not only is annoying and takes I really want to like this game. I've been thinking hard about what's making it feel unsatisfying, and I wanted to write this while it's still in early access and while I still have hope the devs might act on some of this. 1. It's not that runs take too long, it's that they FEEL too long. Nothing new or exciting happens from run to run. Players want to feel powerful, which means you need to give them opportunities both to acquire power and to use it. Get us to the action faster. Get us to the moments where our choices matter. Create more moments of excitement and delight, and make rare things actually feel rare. + What if, instead of choosing a single monster in town and then summoning another at the start of a run, you offered a choice of 3 pairs of monsters before you began? What if each monster came with a pre-assigned random trait from their pool? + What if we also skipped the first level of the pilgrimage path entirely? You'd be putting players ahead with a far more interesting beginning choice. 2. Exploration feels like a chore. It needs to be more dynamic. Combing a map just to find the last 3g shiny spot isn't fun. You already have breakable assets in the world. Follow Zelda's lead and let coins drop out of them occasionally. Think about how exciting it was to see a big red rupee appear out of a broken pot when Link smashed it. Use fewer shiny spots, but make each one matter. Either give players a real reason to care about the map, or lean into the Slay the Spire model and cut the exploration altogether. + What if some enemies had a patrol path and if they spot you then you begin the fight staggered? + What if enemies rarely dropped trophies you could collect and display in town — and destroying a trophy gave your next run a unique effect? + What if there were rare hidden walls with a meaningful reward inside? + What if a rare chest could appear sometimes containing a trophy, premium currency, or a permanent upgrade? 3. Combat is somehow both too complex and one-dimensional. One-dimensional: your party quickly gets optimized into following the same pattern every fight. Monsters get locked into single priority actions, so you're making the same choices each round regardless of what you're up against. Too complex: there are a lot of systems interacting in ways that aren't clearly communicated, so it's genuinely hard to know what will happen. Monster perks often fade into background noise until they suddenly matter. The worst offender is the interrupt mechanic: you ready an ability, the target shows it will be interrupted, you fire... and it doesn't interrupt. Then a burn or sidekick trigger steals the interrupt instead. The choice I made based on what the screen showed me turned out not to be the choice that actually happened. Fights also just feel same-y because enemies don't have enough variety in how they're defeated. Your strategy rarely needs to change. You may as well give players a synergy score and let fights auto-resolve (which isn't fun, so don't). Boss fights are the one place where scaling power gets to shine. + What if you sometimes encountered mini-bosses in biomes? + What if fights weren't always 3v3? + What if perks were displayed as icons under health bars, separate from the buff/debuff clutter? 4. The lore and dialogue is exhausting. Exposition dumps are outdated. The best lore is mysterious and discoverable. Presenting a perfect opportunity to make map exploration more rewarding without just handing out more power. You don't have to say things outright; players care more when they feel like they earned the discovery. Hollow Knight is the obvious example: its lore is endlessly compelling precisely because it's subdued. You encounter things that make you curious. You don't get a wiki article read back to you. If you're going to have this much dialogue, make it about the relationships between characters. Give NPCs personality rather than making them lore-dispensing machines. + What if lore interactibles on maps were rarer and more significant? Instead of Siriux telling the player what he knows, what if he described it as if the player were there? Invoke a feeling, hint at a connection to your monsters? + What if something special triggered when you encountered a lore moment with the right monster in your party? 5. Progression peaks too fast. It's very easy to buy out most of the town upgrades, and once you do, rewards stop feeling like rewards. I want to open a shop and get excited to try something in my next run. There's some of that, just not enough. It's roguelike 101: make the baseline harder, and front-load the power curve with more direct, exciting rewards early on. Your first run should rarely be winnable. You quickly get stronger, push your progression further, until you settle into a steadier core loop where power jumps are fewer and farther between. That dopamine cycle is what hooks people in the early runs. 6. Town and its NPCs need more life. After a run, I cross the bridge and go talk to the Knight. I've bought out his inventory for a while now, but I still open it every time, hoping something new appeared. I'm certain I'm not alone in that. What if you could buy something from the Knight that guaranteed he'd appear in your first level? From the Witch, something that guaranteed your first reroll included Maverick Skills? From the Cook, a guaranteed set of options when you find him on a run? + What if NPCs had a rotating inventory so there's always something new to consider. + What if the Knight sold something that guaranteed he'd appear in the first level? + What if the Witch sold something that guaranteed your first reroll included Maverick Skills? + What if you introduced quest lines? Quest lines could put major progression upgrades behind more interesting mechanisms than purchasing with currency. They can give personality to NPCs, be a vehicle for giving more lore, and present opportunities to make exploration or each run feel different. The Cook quest line concept writes itself: Stage 1: Craft a memento for an ooze → unlock monster meals between biomes Stage 2: Complete a unique run with a full party of 3 oozes → unlock tier 2 monster meals Stage 3: Complete a Heroic run starting with an ooze carrying a quest item it can't replace → unlock tier 3 monster meals (or a unique bonus) The town is full of NPCs and things to look at that have nothing to do and no reason to interact with. That's a lot of wasted potential. I'll continue playing the game through early access and will be excited to try out new content and features as they're released. As it stands now, I just get bored with the game pretty quickly after trying to get into it again.

A very decent turn-based creature collection game. A lot of them are either boring, overwhelming you with creatures, or very unimaginative in terms of designs; this one is decent -- and not the simplest party-based RPG/roguelite in the world. It will give you a decent challenge without distracting too much with plot and the likes. Also, shinies have mildly different abilities!

Definitely time to give this one a strong endorsement. The makers of Monster Sanctuary have really done a great job with this title and made something unique and challenging here. I love being able to have the feel of a creature collector on a roguelike platform and the depth of the strategic play is really high here. There is a ton of versatility to the way you can build your teams and there a lot of viable ways to play. Every single one of my runs have turned out with very different teams and decisions and they've really hit the target with making the runs feel very distinct. With the current state of the game, this variety is found in the ways that you build your teams. The boss fights at this stage of development are not as varied. Finally - I will call out that this game is pretty difficult on balance. Most players are going to be taking some losses while learning this title. There are accessibility settings to pull the difficulty back, but for me it is a feature to have a game that punishes you for not playing well and I am enjoying the challenge that this game offers.

其实游戏整体的体验比较接近《星际反叛军》，甚至可以说这就是星际反叛军的宝可梦版本，我觉得还是可以打个好评的。 我觉得最大的缺点或者说最让人不舒服的地方其实是宠物只能一次性替换没有一个临时的备战空间，装备也没有，这就导致整个游戏玩起来非常死板和看运气，同时奶妈的必须性又进一步加强了这种死板，本来就三个位置，然后一个位置你还必须得留出来给奶妈，也就是只剩下两个位置是给你构筑用的，这就很扯蛋了。。。 好评只是因为没有中评。

刚开始玩的时候非常兴奋的。 优点很多： 包括怪物之间技能的联动爽感，通过运营做到一回合多动+主动技能的击溃，还有看到新怪物和异色（[b] 是的，这游戏有异色[/b]）的兴奋。每个怪物都有不错的攻击和技能动画 总体很不错的游戏 缺点则如下：： 1，制作组对地图的执念颇深，每一关都有例如隐藏金币等地图探索的要素。虽然事件等会在地图标注，但也意味着不把地图全角落跑一遍，就拿不全金币（对强迫症很不友好）。但地图又比较大，且还有高台设定，难免会有大量重复时间 2，延续第一点，因为每一关地图都比较大，加上每一关约有二三次的战斗，会让一局的时间大大延长。由于构筑会在中期就大致成型，后期的战斗台的战斗逻辑和套路就重复使用，让人很有疲倦感。其次，虽然战斗可以通过绕道避免，但不战斗就没有经验和金币，还是避无可避 总结起来就是：很有趣也很疲倦的游戏 看得出来，制作组对这款游戏非常上心。愿在后续更新能变得更好

Fun game ruined by the dialogue; it's like they wanted to fuse Buddhism, postmodernism, and hyper-progressivism altogether into this profound and thought provoking narrative, but it's just obnoxious word slop that's bereft of reasoning. It starts off unnoticed or subtle but comes on overwhelmingly aggressive as time goes on. By midgame you're always getting lectured about the bigotry and ignorance of humans, who once enslaved the wonderful and diverse monsterkin, or about the need of people (humans) to set aside their privilege and see things through the experience of others before they judge, because seemingly the only truly bad act in life is intolerance (even when the game also tells you there is no good or bad/right or wrong in life because it all comes from the same essence). There are an unbearable amount of individual characters with 'they/them' pronouns, which by the way makes the script utterly confusing to anyone who speaks regular English... Honestly it feels like the dialogue was written by an undergraduate from Berkley with a degree in the negative effects of European colonialism on animal sexuality. I loved monster sanctuary and had high hopes for this game, but I'm just too put off by the script. You could just say, 'why not just skip the dialogue and only play the game?' Sure, and I may do that to get to the end out of nostalgia for monster sanctuary. But without the negative review I feel like that just incentivizes these types of people to continue ruining video games by forcing their nonsensical and anti-reality beliefs into literally everything. I'm old enough to remember what happened to the Dragon Age series, and if there is no pushback from the video game community, every game will be a Veilguard at this point.

This game had been appearing in my queue, it was on sale, reviews were decent. I looked at it and thought "Oh, so it's like Wizard of Legend + creature collecting? I can dig that." Besides I hadn't found anything else during the last steam sale that I was really into, and just wanted to come away from it with something. Maybe I should've just let the sale slide and kept my $20. The problems with this game can be tied to one key word: Progression. Interestingly, I mean this in three ways: gameplay progression, plot progression, and political progression. Gameplay: I did binge-play this game for a few days, I will give it that much. I did have to crank up the combat speed in settings to offset how slow it felt, but otherwise in many ways I enjoyed the tactical RPG system, which was sort of a combo of various other systems I'd seen implemented, between its emphasis on buffs/debuffs, breaking mechanics, and points-based skill usage. That being said, a lot of battles end up turning into a grind when you just don't have the means to quickly or efficiently stagger foes. Against bosses, staggering feels especially unrewarding. The concepts are all there, I think, they just lack proper execution. Perhaps in time, since this is still early access, the devs will do something to make each encounter more diverse and fast-paced. Right now though, it feels very grind-y. And the bosses (the two that I have been able to encounter, anyway) are way too strong and have ironically godlike mechanics. Plot: Wait, what? There's a plot to this game? I never would've guessed. There's just no background, no proper exposition, no context; characters reference other characters and you just have NO CLUE who or what they are talking about. It's like you went out to lunch with your new friend and your friend's childhood friend, and the two of them practically share their own unique language and you are left on the sidelines. Political: Okay seriously, even to many people on the left, this game has WAAAAY too many they/them pronouns. Forget the political statement you're trying to make or the worldview you are attempting to represent; this is just really bad for storytelling. Again with the plot problems. I reached my limit of -trying- to comprehend what was going on when this old aethermancer ghost appeared and started chatting with the protagonist after I got WIPED by that beetle boss guy, and there is just NO WAY to piece sense together from their conversation. Also my limit for playing the game in its current state, for all of the above reasons. I do want to like this game. I like roguelikes and I like creature collecting, and in theory I like them both together. This game just needs some work done. I do hope the developers pay attention to everything players are saying about the early access version.

Overall an ok game, but pretty repetitive and very slow with adding new content. There are spots of dialogue that are extremely awkward shoehorned in politics that really make me question the judgement of the devs.

This game is phenomenal. I’ve seen people make comparisons to Pokemon, and that truly does Aethermancer a disservice. Incredible amount of challenge and depth of strategy makes it so addicting. Subtle lore in the background that adds to the game without being bloated is a nice touch. Scratches the same itch that Slay the Spire or Darkest Dungeon does for me.

接近60的售价，内容待完善，相比前作怪物圣所，售价偏高，内容更少，深度更浅；设计层面上有些优秀，但也有瑕疵。总的来说，是一部体量较小的精品游戏，我会支持。 我的建议如下： 1.为现有职业增加能力： 以 “以太驯兽师”为例，这个角色无法有效利用灵魂，而且无法提供额外经验（驯兽师听起来应该比其他职业训练出的怪兽等级更高）,新能力为在召唤祭坛用灵魂获取经验会比较合理。建议开放特性数量上限为5，不然更高等级如10级就没有意义了。 以太炼金师前期腐化太高，建议新能力开局多发一包护盾粉尘，炼金有以太残渣粉尘也很合理！ 新职业如果是是怪兽融合，那可玩性会非常高，能增加不少新怪物。无论是yu-gi-oh！还是赛尔号，怪兽的融合总是让人兴致高涨！ 2.怪物和流派强度 娜迦、斯芬克斯很强，泛用性也很高，我不是说要削弱它们，而是很多怪兽需要增强，或许刚刚说的融合能解决这一问题； 特性“完美锋刃”搭配行为“火焰穿刺”的强击流派输出很高，而且常与护盾挂钩。建议增强力量流派和暴击流派！这两个有护盾标签的太少，太容易累计大量腐化了，残响3难度没有护盾玩起来太难受！ 3.局内问题 第1点，二层的复活法阵只能复活阵亡怪兽，这很蠢。因为怪物阵亡的对局完全无法进行到遇见复活法阵，而遭遇复活法阵的玩家已经流派成型，没有怪兽阵亡，也没有办法获利。 第2点，炼金森林地图怪物强度过高，比朝圣之路难了太多！大量虚弱堆叠导致玩家打不出伤害，队伍会被严重消耗状态，建议削弱炼金森林怪物的血量或者减少敌方怪物以太获取。 第3点，战斗过程中，3只宠物行动完直接就变成对手回合了！我建议给主角增加基础行动（如生成1随机以太），主角和宠物4次个单位全部行动完之后才到对首回合。（e.g.我想用道具"指挥棒"再为主力怪兽提供再行动，但是最后一只怪兽行动结束，直接就到对手回合，我没有使用道具的时机） 4.bug反馈 炼金森林青铜狮的灵魂绑定虚影，有时会出现在第二层的图层； 战斗中的敌方多段伤害的行动，伤害预警显示，有时只显示第一段伤害结算的结果。（如敌方打击2*3，我方护盾4，实际结算是会打破护盾的，但是显示剩余1护盾值，是承受第一次打击的结果）。
好玩，build类型很多，希望不断推出新怪兽，拓展新地图，建议怪兽本体跟异化版本作出区别，尤其是核心被动，这样会更好玩。
It's a decent game but I think it really suffers being a roguelike. Feels more like a deck builder instead of a creature collector in practice because of the roguelike elements.

The combat system, sheer amount of variety, art, and music are awesome. There's a huge depth to the strategy where I feel like the team building strategy is just starting to click 20 hours in. I also like the characters. I appreciate how they're all quirky in unique ways.

The degree of synergy it's possible to curate reminds me of Astral Ascent. There's a lot of room for experimentation and replayability just to try out different combinations of traits and effects. Really fun.

An absolute gem of a turn-based roguelite! It has a plethora of interesting systems and a lot of challenges to overcome. Honestly, all that you have to know is that the most upvoted negative review of this game has 80h+ played on it at review time and played another 10hs after that. The game is that good. I'm not really into creature collectors or pixel-art but this game is great as a team building turn based roguelie! Every monster has a signature trait and a couple of types that define it (tank, weakness, shield - for instance). You build a team of 3, level them up with skills and powerful traits. On top of that you have strong equipments to use and summoner items. That's a _ton_ of possible combinations and strategies to go on. I'll also say that all the monsters feel strong/viable and have a good design both in abilities and visual appearance. It's really a great game to fire up for a run. Runs exceedingly well on the Steam Deck. It's cool to get into. The game is difficult, you can wipe on your first encounter if you're not careful and even the normal encounters stay difficult later into the game. You have a lot of strategic possibilities to overcome these challenges. You also have a good amount of meta progression, some upgrades can be bought in town for currency and using a monster also gains it "worthiness" which makes that specific monster type stronger. You can even "catch" the bosses which feels very cool. If I had to put a "beware" sign up around systems it'd be these: * many monsters have escalating mechanics, i.e. after some turns they might one shot one of your monsters (who die for the entire run), the health system is also interesting as you basically get permanent damage from strong hits so you start combat with less than max HP (but you can heal up during combat again). All of this together means you need a good amount of defensive utility, while you don't want the combat to go on too long (as the enemies also become stronger/you take more damage). * the exploration on the map is lackluster to me, i.e. I could do without it and just go combat to combat, it feels like it's pretty much only there to show off the admittedly pixel-art * the final boss feels a bit too easy - or rather, most of the time I get to him, I manage to kill him. This might just be a factor of filtering my other runs out before on normal encounters or other bosses if they are too weak. But really, overall a great game I cna highly recommend, esp. if you love turn-based combat and roguelites. I'm eager to see what more content the devs will add!

I super love this little roguelike creature battler. The art and creature designs are immaculate. The balance is overall decent but rough in a few spots. Obviously the game needs more content, which is on the way. Also, I'd argue that the game could use more meta progression upgrades. It doesn't take long to max those out and it's not like they are really making you all that powerful. They are completely missing out on the power fantasy side of the roguelike genre, but that's just a minor complaint. I've still really been enjoying it. My only big complaint is the limited availability at shrines to choose poke---- er, I mean, monsters. So, you get to choose your first monster but your second and third are just up to what is available at the shrine which is usually only 1-3 choices. That's pretty rough for putting together a good party composition that has dps plus healers plus good coverage of the different elements. I'd be okay with this if I could swap out creatures freely at future monster shrines, but here's the issue. When you do that, it salvages the item they have instead of transfering it over to the new monster and the new monster gets less xp than the previous one and you're still spending a monster soul. This is a terrible oversight that can make it very difficult to get a good group composition. I've gotten to the point where if the first monster choices I get aren't great then I just auto restart because otherwise it's a waste of my time. I don't think you should be punished for swapping out monsters because it's still costing you a monster soul anyway. Then it can revolve more around managing your monster soul spending, instead of just relying on pure rng to get a good party. All that being said, the game is still a lot of fun and has crazy good potential. Really looking forward to seeing it in its finished state.
